original_question: If X is an elliptically connected complete Kahler manifold, must its fundamental group pi_1(X) be almost abelian; or at least almost nilpotent, meaning that it contains an abelian, respectively nilpotent, subgroup of finite index?
target_in_paper: §3, 3.1, CONJECTURE on elliptically connected Kähler manifolds, p. 18. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9506006))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core statement very closely: it has the correct hypothesis that X is a complete Kähler manifold, the correct conclusion that pi_1(X) should be almost abelian, and it also preserves the paper’s weaker fallback version asking at least for almost nilpotence, with the finite-index subgroup interpretation stated correctly. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9506006))
missing_details: The paper-specific definition of “elliptically connected” is missing: for any two points x,y in X, they must be connectible by a finite chain of holomorphic images of non-hyperbolic curves and of complex tori. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9506006))

The phrase “non-hyperbolic curves” is not merely informal here: immediately before the conjecture the paper notes that an irreducible smooth quasiprojective curve C is non-hyperbolic if and only if pi_1(C) is abelian. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9506006))

The conjecture is phrased as one statement with a stronger form and a weaker form (“almost abelian” or, more weakly, “almost nilpotent”), rather than as two unrelated questions. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9506006))

To make the question fully stand-alone, it should say explicitly that the chain is finite and that the condition applies to every pair of points x,y in X. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9506006))

It is worth preserving the Kähler hypothesis exactly as stated, because the paper immediately remarks that Kählerness is essential and that non-Kähler compact complex examples can fail even the weaker form. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9506006))

The original conjecture should not be broadened to the author’s subsequent speculative enlargement involving meromorphic images of tori or quasi-compact complex manifolds with abelian fundamental groups; those are mentioned only as possible extensions, not as the target conjecture itself. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9506006))
refined_question: Let X be a complete Kähler manifold that is elliptically connected in the following sense: for every pair of points x,y in X, there exists a finite chain of holomorphic images of non-hyperbolic irreducible smooth quasiprojective curves and of complex tori joining x to y. Must the fundamental group pi_1(X) be almost abelian; or at least, in the weaker form stated in the paper, must pi_1(X) be almost nilpotent, i.e. contain an abelian, respectively nilpotent, subgroup of finite index?
justification: The draft is aimed directly at the exact conjecture stated in §3, item 3.1 of arXiv:alg-geom/9506006. The main repair needed was to restore the paper’s precise definition of “elliptically connected,” because that term is carrying the real geometric content of the hypothesis here. I also kept the paper’s exact stronger/weaker formulation and did not broaden the question to neighboring remarks about almost solvability or enlarged notions of connectedness, since those are not the official conjecture. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9506006))
